topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I stood there, the words hanging in the air between us, my childhood best friend staring back at me with an apologetic frown. "I don't remember you," they said, and the room seemed to grow quieter, the usual hum of life outside now a distant echo. I nodded, a slow, deliberate motion, accepting the weight of those words. It was strange, how a piece of my past, so vivid to me, could have vanished for them. Yet, there was no rush, no immediate need to fill the silence or force a connection. We simply stood, letting the years and memories settle around us, a new kind of understanding beginning to take shape.
